critical_code_review_comments: core/chunk_upload.py — disk-backed under /tmp/jelcos_uploads with TTL=1h and 25 MB cap; single-pod-safe; meta.json holds the original filename; assemble() strips a defensive data: prefix and base64-decodes; clean idempotent.
routes/uploads.py — Pydantic body model, get_current_user auth, KeyError → 404 with a clear user message; tags=[Uploads]; clean.

routes/file_import.py — handles BOTH upload_id and legacy file_b64; chunk_upload.discard() called on success + on the chunked-error path so /tmp doesn't leak; MAX_BYTES=8MB still enforced on the assembled raw; comment confirms the 10 MB ingress cap motive.

routes/financial_model.py — 4 export endpoints reuse _load_for_export() (ownership-scoped); StreamingResponse with proper Content-Disposition attachment + filename; _slug() sanitises model name. CMA endpoints invoke compute_cma_extras for the RBI-style working-capital workbook. seed-from-file uses an allow-list of 13 numeric keys with float coercion — robust against malformed AI output.
frontend/src/utils/chunkUpload.ts — CHUNK_CHARS=512 KB (≤ nginx 1 MB default body limit); per-chunk timeout 60s; tiny and correct.

frontend/app/tools/financial-model.tsx — fm-export-* buttons correctly gated on model?.id with a 'Save the model first…' hint; downloadAuthedFile handles web (blob download) AND native (FileSystem + Sharing) — clean cross-platform.

context_for_next_testing_agent: POST /api/uploads/init returns {upload_id} (string). POST /api/uploads/chunk requires {upload_id, index, total?, chunk_b64} and returns {ok:true, received_bytes:len(chunk_b64)}. Frontend uses CHUNK_CHARS=512*1024 = base64 string length per chunk (NOT raw bytes). File-import endpoint POST /api/file-import/decision/{decision_id} accepts EITHER file_b64 OR upload_id; on success it discards the chunk session. Financial-model export URLs are /api/financial-models/{id}/export/{investor|cma}.{pdf|xlsx} — all require an OWNED, SAVED model and return StreamingResponse with attachment Content-Disposition. AI seed/extract endpoints can legitimately return 400 (no LLM configured) / 402 (out of credits) / 422 (no extractable data) — the test suite skips those branches so the chunked-upload pipeline itself is what's under test.
rca_of_issue: Original P0: POST /api/file-import/decision/{id} sent the full base64 PDF in one ~7-10 MB JSON body, which the kube ingress rejected with 413 before reaching FastAPI. Fix shipped: new chunked-upload pipeline (core/chunk_upload + routes/uploads) lets the client send <1 MB chunks that the proxy never blocks; the server reassembles on demand. Verified directly by uploading a ~1.4 MB raw payload in 4 chunks of ~512 KB base64 each → all chunks 200, no 413, downstream file-import accepted the upload_id and merged factors/options into a real decision.
